Across eight embedded iridium and osmium compounds, ligand-active XMS-CASPT2 places the K$_2$OsCl$_6$ centroid within 0.5~meV of a RIXS maximum while splitting its nearly degenerate reference triplet by 2.54~meV, and matched OpenMolcas 26.10 controls retain the bare-anion sensitivities. Independent BAGEL calculations isolate contraction dependence in a three-state spin-free model: on the same reference, replacing SS--SR with MS--MR reduces the symmetry-defined E-block splitting from 0.448~meV to $4.67\times10^{-5}$~meV. Native reconstruction, reference symmetry, representation invariance, sensitivity controls and comparison with fitted spectral features or magnetic response provide an ordered validation procedure whose tests constrain different properties of the Hamiltonian.

papers.title: Phase-resolved spin-orbit exciton transfer with dressed quantum encodings
papers.abstract: A quantum simulation of a material runs on a register much smaller than the electronic problem behind it, and the map between the two decides what a measured correlation means. We study this map for spin--orbit exciton transfer across an Ir--Ir bond of a LiIrF$_6$-derived model. Exact references show that a bare product-state encoding has an amplitude floor above a 0.02 state tolerance at sampled times, whereas a polar-dressed encoding lowers the ten-window projected error from 0.320 to $3.54\times10^{-4}$. Three-CZ axial and two-CZ transverse circuits, run on IBM Kingston in eight acquisitions with 1.6 million shots, resolve population transfer together with both quadratures of the intersite coherence. Raw half-transfer Bell-projector scores reach 0.935 in two independent acquisitions, and on a second bond a coherent arm with lower bound 0.871 is separated from a matched dephased control. Across 2,520 model points, adaptive spectral encodings meet fixed accuracy targets with explicit dimension costs.

papers.title: Edge spin generalization for quantum Hall Laughlin droplets with elliptic shapes
papers.abstract: It is known that quasiparticles in the bulk of quantum Hall systems possess an emergent spin, which satisfies a spin-statistics relation. Recent results show that this spin can fractionalize: a quasiparticle spin in the bulk induces an opposite edge spin on the boundary. So far, the edge spin has only been studied in the simplest possible geometries, where the boundary is either circular or straight, without considering that a generic confining potential could give the droplet a non-symmetric shape. Yet, the value of the edge spin is not dictated by symmetry, but by topology: it is expected that the specific shape of the edge should not matter. In this work, we therefore generalize the edge spin to elliptically shaped droplets. We consider two different generalizations of the edge spin and test them on a family of elliptic Laughlin states introduced in the present work. The first, most straightforward, generalization is based on the properties of the single-particle orbitals for the elliptic confining potential. We show that this proposal applies to non-interacting states. The second proposal is based on the emergent properties of the quantum fluid. We show that this proposal also applies to interacting states, making it the suitable definition of the edge spin in the elliptic case. Our work demonstrates that it is possible to define an edge spin for Laughlin fluids with a non-trivial shape.

papers.title: Thermally Hysteretic Room-Temperature Nonlinear Hall Effect in Bulk EuTe4
papers.abstract: The nonlinear Hall effect (NLHE) is a novel transport phenomena and shows great potential applications of future electronics. However, the realization of a giant and tunable NLHE in bulk materials at room temperature remains elusive. Here, we report a NLHE in bulk EuTe4 single crystals, which persists up to 400 K and exhibits pronounced thermal hysteresis behaviors. The ratio of nonlinear Hall voltages during warming and cooling processes is about 4.7 at 340 K. Such phenomena could be related to the inversion-symmetry-broken charge density wave state in EuTe4. These findings demonstrate bulk EuTe$_4$ as a promising platform for tunable nonlinear electronic devices at room temperature.

papers.title: Observing Enhanced Entanglement in an Ising Quantum Register Beyond Weak Measurement
papers.abstract: Measurements often yield a disentangled quantum state which is the most probable measurement outcome while the measurement outcomes with enhanced entanglement could be exponentially less probable or absent. Higher probability in measurement outcomes with enhanced entanglement is virtue in experimental observation of enhance entanglement in post-selected or Born-rule measurements with less resources in noisy quantum devices. We develop a periodic measurement sampling(PMS) protocol in the framework of uniform matrix product states. Using PMS, we identify a peak enhancement of entanglement in a uniform post-measurement state whose probabilistic outcome can be maximized by optimizing a measurement super-cell. A measurement super-cell is the smallest repeating building block of qubits defined by the measurement density, external field strength and exchange interactions between quantum register and ancilla qubits. The above prediction based on a classical description of the many-body quantum state is demonstrated in a quantum computing experiment in a loop of quantum register qubits with Ising interactions in the presence of transverse magnetic field. Further, we show the scalability of predictions of the periodic measurement sampling protocol in the thermodynamic limit to finite size systems. Especially, we present a rescaling ansatz which would enable predicting the possibility of observing enhanced entanglement in finite size systems.

papers.title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
papers.abstract: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.

papers.title: Controlled Magnon Chirality and Its Reversal by Anisotropy in Altermagnetic FeF$_2$
papers.abstract: In altermagnets, the exchange symmetry of two mutually compensating magnetic sublattices permits spin-polarized electronic bands and chirality-split magnon bands. Because these effects have opposite signs in domains related by time reversal, magnetic-domain control is essential for their observation and utilization. Using half-polarized neutron diffraction, we demonstrate that we can control magnetic domain imbalance in a single crystal of FeF$_2$ by field cooling, and we relate this response to the established piezomagnetism in this material. Our half-polarized inelastic neutron scattering measurements directly resolve the altermagnetic splitting of chiral magnon bands. Strikingly, we observe a clear reversal of chirality near $\mathbf{Q}=(0.5,0.5,1)$, where the altermagnetic exchange splitting vanishes and no chirality is expected in a nonrelativistic exchange model. This reversal of the chirality is well explained by the presence of a transverse component of the single-ion anisotropy tensor, which rotates between Fe sublattices related by the crystal's altermagnetic $4_2$ screw symmetry. These results allow us to resolve fine features of the spin Hamiltonian for FeF$_2$ and show how symmetry-governed relativistic anisotropy can reshape altermagnetic spin dynamics, as well as providing an avenue for control of magnetic domains and the net chiral response.

papers.title: Vestiges of magnon fractionalization in the quasi-two-dimensional quantum magnet rouaite Cu$_2$(NO$_3$)(OH)$_3$ with alternating ferro- and antiferromagnetic $S=\frac{1}{2}$ chains
papers.abstract: Ferro- and antiferromagnetic quantum spin chains host qualitatively distinct elementary excitations --- magnons ($S=1$, bosonic quasiparticles) and spinons ($S=\frac{1}{2}$, fractionalized quasiparticles), respectively. Weakly coupled networks of both chain types therefore provide an ideal platform for exploring spinon-magnon coupling and the hybridization of sharp magnon modes with spinon continua. Here we investigate the spin-excitation spectrum of the frustrated quantum magnet rouaite, Cu$_2$(NO$_3$)(OH)$_3$ --- a model realization of weakly coupled ferro- and antiferromagnetic Cu$^{2+}$ spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ chains. The frustrated interchain interactions, while weaker than the dominant intrachain exchange, are sufficient to stabilize a long-range-ordered state that is not reproduced by classical calculations. Neutron spectroscopy reveals a spectrum of well-defined spin waves associated with both types of chains, with clear signatures of hybridization but no observable spinon continuum. Certain magnon branches resulting from this hybridization exhibit substantial broadening near the zone center. We attribute this to vestiges of spinon fractionalization persisting partway through the dimensional crossover from isolated quantum spin chains to a 2D network of frustrated spins.

papers.title: Charge and spin orders of the generalized Wigner crystal phases at fractional fillings in twisted MoTe$_2$: unrestricted Hartree-Fock and variational Monte Carlo studies
papers.abstract: Recent experiments have revealed interaction-driven insulating states at various fractional fillings of twisted bilayer MoTe$_2$. Many of these insulating states are believed to be generalized Wigner crystals (GWC) condensed in the background of triangular moir$\acute{e}$ lattice. In this work, we focus on revealing the charge and spin order of the insulating states at 4/3 and 3/2 hole fillings over a range of twist angles and applied displacement fields using unrestricted Hartree-Fock (HF) and variational Monte Carlo (VMC) methods. We find that, at 4/3 filling for low twist angles the charge ordered ground state is valley-polarized (VP), characterized by weak charge delocalization approaching the classical limit. Application of the displacement field induces layer-polarization and suppresses the charge fluctuations even further. In contrast, at 3/2 filling, the VP phase exhibits signatures of a two-component GWC phase, which is particularly robust at finite displacement field. Additionally, by increasing the twist angle one pushes the system into an intervalley-coherent (IVC) phase, which is found to be fluctuation-dominated. Our VMC-based analysis shows that the correlation energy is negligible in the VP phase, which is consistent with its classical nature. However, the IVC phase shows significant gain in correlation energy, which is dominated by the nonlocal correlations captured by the Jastrow factors, while the local Gutzwiller factors play a minor role.

papers.title: Two correlation scales in homogeneous density-matrix functionals: the Müller logarithm and the sharp Csányi--Arias asymptotics
papers.abstract: We resolve the exact high-density correlation scales and coefficients of the three-dimensional translation-invariant, spin-symmetric Müller and Csányi--Arias corrected Hartree--Fock (CHF) functionals, settling long-standing numerical observations of Müller overcorrelation and apparently vanishing CHF correlation. In Hartree units, for fixed spin multiplicity $q$ and Fermi momentum $k=(6π^2ρ/q)^{1/3}$, their gains per particle over the filled Fermi sea satisfy \[ D_{\rm M}(k)=\frac{3}{4π^2}\log k+O(1),\qquad D_{\rm CHF}(k)=12e^{-1/2-π^2/8} k^2e^{-π^{3/2}\sqrt{k}}(1+o(1)). \] The Müller proof retains the occupation cap and identifies the factor-of-two cancellation between exchange defect and energy gain. For periodic Müller jellium, convexity and translation--spin averaging allow a global minimizer to be chosen invariant and identify the unrestricted thermodynamic energy with the homogeneous spin-symmetric value. The CHF upper bound follows from a deterministic comparison built from the explicit Hartree--Fock dispersion, combining a full Birman--Schwinger bound with one-sided norms and completion of the square; a number-preserving trial state provides the matching lower bound, and the retained remainder yields weighted $L^2$ convergence of the occupation defect without analyzing the self-consistent gap. We also prove existence for both functionals and uniqueness of the CHF minimizer. Relative to the unpolarized quantum high-density benchmark, Müller has a larger logarithmic coefficient, providing quantitative evidence for the conjectured Müller lower-bound property, whereas CHF misses the logarithmic scale altogether. The quantum benchmark is not used in either functional proof.

papers.title: Classical weak antilocalization in electron hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Weak localization is strongly suppressed in electron hydrodynamics, where frequent electron--electron collisions rapidly dephase the Cooperon. Nevertheless, disorder can still produce a logarithmic correction to the bare hydrodynamic resistivity. We show that spatial fluctuations of the momentum-relaxation rate generate a classical memory kernel through the diffusive return of transverse momentum. In two dimensions, this return is logarithmic, as in weak localization, but involves a single shear propagator rather than quantum interference. Conservation laws and positivity of dissipation fix its antilocalizing sign: the return reduces momentum relaxation and hence the bulk resistivity. Unlike quantum weak localization, the logarithm is cut off by momentum relaxation and has a viscosity-dependent amplitude. For temperature-independent impurity friction, the resistivity correction scales as $-T^2\ln(T_ξ/T)$ in a Fermi liquid and $-T\ln(T_ξ/T)$ in a Planckian metal. In channels, the return competes with viscosity renormalization, and a width scan separates the two effects.

papers.title: Quantum Fluctuations drive Emerging Bosonic Quantum Phases in a Moiré Flatband Superconductor
papers.abstract: Quantum fluctuations play a central role in superconductors by mediating the interactions that promote electron pairing and controlling the phase coherence required for macroscopic condensation. Thus far, understanding the interplay between quantum fluctuations and superconductivity remains challenging in unconventional superconductors. Here, we establish quantum phase fluctuations as the organizing principle linking superconductivity and Bose-insulating quantum criticality in a moiré flatband superconductor of alternating twisted trilayer graphene (ATTG). Superconductivity is optimal near half-filling of the moiré flatband and gives way to a density-wave-like resistance peak at high temperatures, in which we observe distinct temperature scales for the pairing (~6 K) and the condensation (~1 K). We observe compelling evidence of a bosonic superconducting quantum phase transition, driven by both out-of-plane and in-plane magnetic fields, with a universal critical resistivity of $R_c =~0.62R_Q$ and finite-temperature scaling of $zν_B = 2.3$, where $R_Q = h/4e^2$ is the quantum resistance for bosons. Strikingly, the observed bosonic insulator shows a nearly quantized resistivity of $R_Q$ that saturates at low temperatures and high magnetic fields, together with a zero-bias peak, a nearly zero Hall resistance, and a logarithmic dependence at higher temperatures. Both the superconductor and the bosonic insulator could be driven into the same critical quantum fluctuation regime dynamically under a large bias. Our results establish moiré flatband as a clean platform for studying unconventional superconductivity and bosonic quantum criticality governed by quantum fluctuations.

papers.title: Evaluate Laughlin spectral gap lower bound in vortexable bands
papers.abstract: Vortexable Chern bands admit exact Laughlin-type zero modes of local parent interactions, but their existence alone does not guarantee a finite excitation gap. Here, we derive a computable, particle-number-independent lower bound on the spectral gap of Laughlin parent Hamiltonians in a class of vortexable bands obtained by multiplying lowest-Landau-level wavefunctions by a spatially varying envelope. The bound depends only on two quantities: the spread of projected orbital normalizations and a lower bound on the weighted local pair repulsion, both determined by one- and two-particle operators. The proof employs an auxiliary fermion-loss construction to control orbital orthogonalization, with an error bounded relative to the interaction energy uniformly in particle number. We demonstrate that Landau-level averaging permits strictly positive gap bounds even under substantial spatial modulation, including envelopes with nodal lines. Beyond the scalar-envelope construction, we extend the analysis to multicomponent orbital textures and deformations of the vortex coordinate. These results establish rigorous gap criteria for Laughlin parent Hamiltonians, providing a foundation for understanding the stability of fractional Chern insulators in vortexable bands.

papers.title: Local gluing classification and bulk-locked clock rings for $\mathbb{Z}_N$ models on a Klein bottle
papers.abstract: We classify local reflection gluings of the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ plaquette model on lattice Klein bottles and solve the obstructed literal seam. Within the monomial far-corner ansatz, all commuting gluings form a family labelled by a unit $u$ of $\mathbb{Z}_N$. They exist for every $N$ at even seam length and, at odd length, exactly when $-1$ is a square modulo $N$. We determine the anyon transport, including exchange seams with $P^2=C$ for charge conjugation $C$, and the relation phases that distinguish an unfrustrated code from a commuting but frustrated Hamiltonian. For the literal gluing, the $2L_x$ noncommuting plaquettes form self-dual clock rings whose sectors are locked by the bulk. This gives an exact reduction of the spectrum to clock-ring spectra, closed-form ring ground energies for $N=2,4$, and a closed-form ground-state degeneracy. We further determine twisted-coefficient homology on the stated surface domains and compare it with logical modules on registered lattice grids; composite dimensions need not give squares of cyclic groups. Dressed-isometry gates and monodromy are reported with their finite-grid scope. Finally, the qudit Gottesman--Knill theorem bounds the computational interpretation: Clifford deformations and Weyl measurements with stabilizer inputs and no external magic states cannot supply a non-stabilizer resource. Charge-conjugation measurements that do supply such states lie outside this operation model. The new results concern explicit seam classification, phase-sensitive consistency and bulk-locked spectra, not a new general no-go theorem or a universal computing architecture.

papers.title: Anyon Proliferation at Self-Triality: From a Lattice Model to Adjoint QCD$_3$
papers.abstract: We study how competitive proliferation among three types of anyons in a self-trial $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory can drive symmetry breaking while preserving part of the topological order. We construct a deformation of the honeycomb color code, a spin model rooted in quantum error correction, with an $S_3$ symmetry that permutes the competing anyons, together with time-reversal and fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2^{(1)}$ one-form symmetries. We propose two dual continuum descriptions of this transition. The bosonic description is a $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_3\times\mathrm{Spin}(8)_{-1}$ Chern-Simons-Higgs theory with a real Higgs field in the $(\mathbf{8}_{\mathrm{adj}},\mathbf{8}_v)$ representation. Fermion-boson duality gives a particularly simple fermionic dual: $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_{3/2}$ QCD$_3$ with a single adjoint Majorana fermion and gauged fermion parity. Both descriptions match the lattice model's unitary symmetries and proposed phase diagram, connecting double-toric-code order to a symmetry-broken phase with residual toric-code order. The transition is described by Higgs condensation and by a Majorana mass changing sign, respectively. The continuum theories are proposed to recover lattice time reversal at criticality. This connection to adjoint QCD$_3$ points to a possible continuous $S_3$-breaking transition from competing anyons, in contrast to the conventional first-order three-state Potts transition from competing local order parameters.

papers.title: Theoretical exploration of ambient-pressure superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate: A strategy of atomic substitution for tuning chemical pressure
papers.abstract: The possibility of ambient-pressure superconductivity in $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$ is theoretically explored via chemical substitution. Using first-principles and many-body calculations, we propose substituting $\mathrm{Ba}$ at the lanthanide site to exert chemical pressure, thereby mitigating the octahedral distortions that suppress superconductivity. Phonon calculations demonstrate the dynamical stability of the high-symmetry tetragonal phase in $\mathrm{La_{3-\it{x}}Ba_{\it{x}}Ni_2O_7}$ at a small doping ratio of $x \sim 0.15$. By applying the fluctuation exchange approximation to an effective model Hamiltonian derived from this stable structure, we calculate the Eliashberg eigenvalue $λ$ to evaluate the relative superconducting transition temperature $T_\mathrm{c}$ to existing unconventional superconductors. We conclude that $s_\pm$-wave superconductivity is likely to emerge, as the required $\mathrm{Ba}$ concentration ($x \sim 0.15$) is sufficiently small to minimize the detrimental suppression of superconductivity induced by hole doping.

papers.title: Entanglement and information dynamics in charged dual-unitary circuits with impurities
papers.abstract: Local parts of a closed, non-equilibrium quantum many-body system can reach stationarity through the buildup of entanglement between different regions. In this paper we investigate how this process is affected by the presence of a quantum impurity that breaks a global symmetry of the bulk. In particular, we study a charged dual-unitary quantum circuit perturbed by a symmetry-breaking, non-dual-unitary gate acting on a spatially fixed pair of sites. In this setup we calculate the entanglement entropy for a subsystem that does not contain the impurity, as well as the mutual information and logarithmic negativity for a bipartite subsystem that straddles the impurity. We obtain exact results in the early time regime for these quantities from the dual unitarity of the bulk system. Beyond this regime, we compute the predictions of the quasiparticle and entanglement membrane pictures, supporting them with exact calculations obtained by taking the corresponding limits of the bulk entangling power. We find that the presence of a symmetry-breaking impurity can lead to a richer behaviour of quantum relaxation, including non-monotonic evolution of the entanglement entropy, a modification of the long-time steady state, and persistent subsystem mutual information and entanglement negativity. This behaviour is understood in terms of long-range correlations generated by scattering from the impurity, and facilitated by the ballistic propagation of the conserved charges.

papers.title: Correlation functions of the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas in equilibrium states: a microscopic approach to space-time asymptotics
papers.abstract: We develop an approximation-free approach to the analysis of form-factor series for the correlation functions of quantum integrable models in the thermodynamic limit and in equilibrium states described by a class of stationary density matrices. This allows us to obtain the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of the correlation functions in thermal equilibrium and in stationary states after a quench, including such states that can be described by generalized Gibbs ensembles. Our approach will be exemplified with the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas or non-linear Schrödinger model. It applies to the correlation functions of all local operators. For the two-point functions of particle-density or particle-current density operators our findings confirm the phenomenological predictions based on generalised hydrodynamics. We extract as well the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of a field- conjugated field correlation function. At present its behaviour is outside the reach of any heuristic method. It is governed by a novel non-linear integral equation that depends on space and time.

papers.title: Mechanical acclimation of bacterial growth and division across generations
papers.abstract: Bacteria frequently encounter mechanical confinement in natural and engineered environments, yet how an abrupt change in mechanical conditions reorganizes growth and division across generations remains poorly understood. Using single-cell time-lapse microscopy, we tracked Escherichia coli across generations following transfer from liquid culture to glass-attached or glass-gel-confined conditions. This mechanical confinement causes an immediate reduction in elongation rate, followed by a multi-generational mechanical acclimation process whose dynamics depend systematically on confinement strength. During this relaxation, division behavior becomes more heterogeneous and cells temporarily depart from canonical adder-like size regulation, exhibiting timer-like correlation signatures. Using a stochastic cell-cycle model that resolves the generation-dependent correlation signatures of different size-control strategies, we show that changes in elongation rate alone cannot account for the observed transition in growth-division coordination. Despite this transient reorganization, the birth-size distribution remains bounded and largely preserves its shape throughout acclimation. Notably, adder-like regulation is restored before the elongation rate fully recovers, revealing distinct relaxation timescales for growth and size-control dynamics. These results establish bacterial size control under mechanical confinement as a dynamical nonequilibrium process in which growth and division can transiently reorganize while global size homeostasis is maintained.

papers.title: Real-Space-RG for the drawups and drawdowns of run-and-tumble trajectories: universality classes for models with space-dependent velocities and switching rates
papers.abstract: For one-dimensional run-and-tumble processes with the two velocities $v_{\pm}(x)$ and the two switching rates $γ_{\pm}(x)$, a given stochastic trajectory is an alternating sequence of local minima and local maxima corresponding to the switching events between the ballistic motions with velocities $v_{\pm}(x) $ in the two directions. The renormalized trajectory at scale $Γ$ is obtained by keeping only the alternating sequence of local minima and local maxima that are separated by drawups and drawdowns of amplitude bigger than $Γ$. Its statistical properties can be analyzed via the generalization of the previous work arxiv:2611.04853 concerning diffusion processes involving arbitrary diffusion coefficients $D(x)$ and Ito forces $F_I(x)$. The main result is that the scale function $s(x)$ of diffusion processes that depends only on the ratio $\frac{F_I(x)}{D(x) } $ is replaced by a pair of scale functions $s_{\pm}(x)$ that depend only on the two ratios $\frac{γ_+( x ) }{v_+( x )}$ and $\frac{γ_-( x ) }{v_-( x )}$. This pair of scale functions $s_{\pm}(x)$ govern the exit probabilities from an interval and determine the universality classes of the renormalized trajectories: all run-and-tumble processes with the same two ratios $\frac{γ_+( x ) }{v_+( x )}$ and $\frac{γ_-( x ) }{v_-( x )}$ share the same statistics of renormalized trajectories. This general framework is illustrated with examples that are compared to their diffusive counterparts : uniform symmetric and asymmetric processes on the whole line $x \in]-\infty,+\infty[$, geometric process on the half-line $x \in]0,+\infty[$, and an exponential functional of the telegraph process with a normalizable steady state.

papers.title: Exact stochastic theory of post-transcriptional gene autoregulation mediated by RNA-binding proteins
papers.abstract: While analytical theories of transcriptional feedback loops have been well established, exact stochastic analyses of post-transcriptional feedback loops remain relatively scarce and are notoriously challenging. Here, we develop an exact theory of post-transcriptional gene autoregulation, in which reversible protein-mRNA binding modulates both translation and mRNA stability. We derive the state-dependent protein burst-size distribution, the steady-state protein number distribution in terms of confluent Heun functions, and an exact criterion for sub-Poissonian fluctuations. By comparing transcriptional and post-transcriptional networks, we reveal a reversal in their relative advantages in noise suppression and rhythm transmission: negative feedback favors post-transcriptional regulation, whereas positive feedback favors transcriptional regulation. Our results reveal how the regulatory pattern fundamentally shapes gene expression fluctuations and dynamic responses.

papers.title: Quantum kinetic uncertainty relations: Role of coherence in current fluctuation bounds
papers.abstract: We present a comparative analysis of three quantum versions of the kinetic uncertainty relation (KUR), which incorporate coherence-dependent corrections to the classical bound. Using a three-level maser heat engine as a paradigmatic quantum thermal machine, we identify the operating regimes in which each formulation provides the tightest constraint on current fluctuations. We further identify tighter, model-specific bounds for two of these formulations, provide numerical support for both, and establish one of them analytically. Introducing ground-state degeneracy, we then demonstrate that noise-induced coherence provides a tunable resource for relocating, enhancing, or suppressing violations of the standard KUR without requiring an additional coherent drive. In particular, it enables violations in regimes where the three-level engine satisfies the classical bound. Our results clarify how distinct quantum KURs account for coherence and constrain the precision of quantum thermal machines.

papers.title: Emulating spatially extended systems using Fourier Neural Operator
papers.abstract: Operator Learning (OL) algorithms approximate underlying mathematical operators by mapping entire classes of input functions to their corresponding solutions. For instance, architectures such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) have been trained on numerical datasets generated by isolated, stiff ionic models to provide a data-driven alternative to traditional numerical integration schemes. However, real-world biological and physical systems typically consist of interconnected spatial units arranged in complex, heterogeneous networks. Motivated by this observation, we generalize this data-driven framework to spatially extended systems defined on diverse graph topologies, ranging from Erdos-Renyi to Barabasi-Albert networks. Furthermore, we evaluate the proposed approach on empirical data, demonstrating its ability to accurately and efficiently model task-oriented neural activity.

papers.title: A Multiobjective Optimization Framework for Sensor Array Design in Magnetocardiography
papers.abstract: Magnetocardiography (MCG) noninvasively measures cardiac magnetic fields. Conventional cryogenic systems use fixed multichannel arrays, whereas room-temperature sensors enable flexible placement to reduce array size and measurement redundancy. The present study aims at developing a scheme to identify the optimal sensor placements by utilizing three methodological sensor optimization frameworks such as physics driven, experimental data driven and a hybrid combination of both. The physics-driven method optimizes continuous planar coordinates using D-optimality, spatial correlation, and leastsquares error. The data-driven method uses measured spatiotemporal fields and pole-geometry metrics, while the hybrid method integrates both approaches. The evaluation is performed using training objective, Pearson correlation, normalized root-meansquare error (NRMSE) and pole separation(mm), orientation(°) and trajectory(mm) errors, where physics-driven optimization identified 16 sensors with a correlation of 0.9914 and an NRMSE of 0.0139, with pole separation, orientation, and trajectory errors of 3.71 mm, 1.38°, and 3.55 mm, respectively. Data-driven optimization shows diminishing improvements beyond 17 sensors, achieving correlation 0.9840, NRMSE 0.0035, and pole errors of approximately 4.30 mm, 1.70°, and 6.80 mm. The hybrid method achieves correlation 0.9945 and NRMSE 0.0201 with 14 sensors, reducing sensor count by 12.5% relative to the physics-driven configuration. Its pole errors of 6.50 mm, 2.31°, and 7.50 mm satisfy the study-defined thresholds, balancing array compactness with magnetic-field morphology preservation. These results show that optimized placement helps alleviate the complexity of data redundancy and enhances the performance of MCG as a routine cost-effective clinical measurement.

papers.title: Foundation Tensor Networks Generalize Across Quantum Lattice Systems
papers.abstract: Neural quantum states and tensor networks have emerged as leading techniques for simulating quantum many-body systems. However, disordered systems remain extremely challenging in both frameworks as they require computation of the ground state for every realization of the disorder. Recently, neural quantum states have been used to construct foundation models that generate the ground state directly from the Hamiltonian. Still, they are hindered by the need to perform extensive sampling to estimate observables. To address these difficulties, we introduce the foundation tensor network (FTN), which uses a neural network to generate the tensor network representation of the ground-state wavefunction from the Hamiltonian. To accelerate training, we develop a technique, called \texttt{GridBP}, based on iterated one-dimensional belief propagation that reduces the cost of computing the energy expectation value to just two tensor contractions. We use FTNs to calculate the critical parameters of the glass transition in the quantum Edwards-Anderson model via finite-size scaling analysis. To facilitate rapid averaging, we use a moment-generating function to evaluate the order parameter, lowering the cost to a single tensor contraction. We obtain high-fidelity estimates for the critical parameters by averaging over 500,000 disorder realizations.

papers.title: Magic of Dicke states: density, cost and yield
papers.abstract: Dicke states are an elementary family of many-body quantum states, consisting of equal superpositions of all configurations of $L$ qubits with $n$ excitations. We show that their magic, as measured by the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), is extensive at every filling $f=n/L$ except half-filling, and we obtain the magic density analytically, together with the subleading terms. In the context of fault-tolerant quantum computation, we also investigate the yield of Dicke states, and find that they can produce on average an extensive number of CCZ states (or $T$ states with a catalyst) at any $0<f<1$. This yield is not self-averaging, but fluctuates from run to run by $O(L)$, as if it were set by a hidden phase shared by all qubits. At half-filling, the SRE grows only logarithmically, while the preparation cost, average yield and relative entropy of magic remain extensive, so that a small SRE does not necessarily signal a weak resource.
